headline: All majors underwater on their 200-day lines; positioning crowded long and funded; whales pulling coins cold while stablecoin float shrinks.
paragraphs: The regime is bearish across the board. Bitcoin, Ethereum, Solana, XRP, BNB, Doge, and Cardano all trade below their 200-day simple moving averages, and not one of them has achieved a golden cross. Bitcoin sits at 63,443.63, down 0.15% in the last 24 hours but up 8.33% over 30 days, a window mismatch that matters: the monthly gain is real, but the week shows almost nothing (down 0.04%), and today is a fresh red print. Ethereum is 1,878.52, down 0.1% on the day, up 19.66% on the month but down 0.17% on the week. This is a market that rallied into late July and has since gone sideways to slightly downward. The rally from the lows has not yet reclaimed the 200-day line for any major asset, and the distribution is consistent: all seven are below trend. This is not a mixed regime; it is a unified one.

Momentum is soft against a weak backdrop. Bitcoin's RSI-14 sits at 45.6 (neutral to slightly oversold), and its MACD is below signal, confirming downward momentum. Ethereum's RSI is 50.7 with MACD also below signal. XRP is the weakest, at RSI 35.5 (oversold) with MACD below signal and the worst weekly performance at negative 7.46%. Three assets do show MACD above signal (SOL, BNB, DOGE), which means their momentum oscillators have ticked higher, but each of these still trades below the 200-day line and each has also failed to generate a golden cross. BNB's RSI is notably elevated at 63.5, suggesting its recent rally (up 11.77% in 30 days, up 3.94% in the week) has pushed momentum into overbought territory. Cardano, despite posting the strongest 30-day gain at 26.67%, is down 3.52% on the week and carries the highest 30-day volatility in the cohort at 59.3%. The picture is: some momentum has returned, but it sits atop a trend that has not yet turned.

Derivatives positioning is heavily long and the cost to hold that bet is rising. Bitcoin's open interest stands at 2.12 billion USD on OKX with a 1.88 long-to-short ratio, meaning nearly two longs for every short. Ethereum's OI is 1.26 billion with a 1.83 ratio. Funding on both is 0.01% per 8-hour period, annualizing to 11%, which is elevated: traders are paying significantly to hold long positions. Over the last 22 hours, Bitcoin saw 636 liquidations (2.65M longs, 1.19M shorts), skewed toward long side pain. Ethereum's 1,143 liquidations over 23 hours ran the other direction (4.28M longs against 5.42M shorts), suggesting shorts caught off guard. Solana's funding is barely positive at 0.0007% (0.7% annualized), the lowest in the set, but its long-to-short ratio is a steep 2.24. XRP and Doge show even more extreme ratios (3.33 and 4.93) with elevated funding (both at 11% and 6.6% annualized), and Doge's liquidations show zero shorts blown out in 18 hours against 890K longs, a sign of one-sided positioning. The macro read: positioning is crowded to the long side, funding is not cheap, and any downturn will hunt stops in that direction.

Whale flows paint a defensive picture. Over the last 48 hours, 236.98 million USD net moved off exchanges, composed of 180.81M BTC (entirely from Kraken in one 128.87M clip) and 56.17M ETH (entirely from Binance). This is cold storage behavior during a period when the market is not panicking (Fear & Greed at 29, within its 30-day range of 25 to 33). Simultaneously, Bitcoin ETF spot flows on 11 August were positive 7.8M but show only one day of same-direction flow; the last five sessions netted positive 346.9M. Ethereum ETF flows on the same date were negative 1.7M (two days of same direction). The signal is mixed on the spot side but clear on the whale side: accumulation into cold storage. Stablecoin float sits at 306.4 billion USD, down 0.98% over 30 days, implying slightly reduced dry powder. The largest stablecoin move saw 169.9M USDT leave Bitfinex against 140M flowing in, another net-off-exchange print. Whales are extracting and holding; stablecoin buyers are not yet stepping in hard.

The Fear & Greed index reads 29 (Fear), the low end of its recent 30-day band (25 to 33). The crowd is afraid. Yet on the tape, the long positioning is elevated, funding is expensive, and the recent month for most assets has been up (BTC 8.33%, ETH 19.66%, BNB 11.77%, ADA 26.67%). This is a divergence. The week-to-week action has gone flat or red, but the month is still green. Whales are moving coins cold, which is either accumulation (confidence) or de-risking (caution); without news or directional conviction, it reads as defense. ETF flows have been bid but without persistence (one day same-direction for Bitcoin, two for Ethereum). The tape is saying: there is no panic, but there is no rush either. The crowd feels fear; the money is moving defensibly.

Watch for a reclaim of the 200-day line on any major asset (the first golden cross would signal trend reversal). Watch funding on Bitcoin and Ethereum: if 0.01% per 8 hours flips negative, long positioning is unwinding. Watch the stablecoin float: if it rises sharply, new dry powder is being deployed. Watch whale flows: a reversal to net inflows back onto exchanges would suggest liquidation or profit-taking at heights. Monitor liquidations: a switch in the dominant side would mean the positioning imbalance is resolving. The regime has held for months; the data today does not show it breaking.
